question: Could you find out the average percentage of the total lifetime sales (LTV) that occur in the first 7 and 30 days after a customer's initial purchase? Also, include the average total lifetime sales (LTV). Please exclude customers with zero lifetime sales. The 7- and 30-day periods should be based on the exact number of hours-minutes-seconds, not calendar days.
sql:
-- Build the main query - fix column alias
WITH customer_first_payment AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        MIN(payment_date) as first_payment_date
    FROM payment
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
customer_payments_with_hours AS (
    SELECT 
        p.customer_id,
        p.amount,
        p.payment_date,
        EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (p.payment_date - cfp.first_payment_date)) / 3600.0 as hours_after_first
    FROM payment p
    JOIN customer_first_payment cfp ON p.customer_id = cfp.customer_id
),
customer_ltv AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        SUM(amount) as total_ltv
    FROM payment
    GROUP BY customer_id
    HAVING SUM(amount) > 0
),
customer_window_payments AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        SUM(CASE WHEN hours_after_first <= 168 THEN amount ELSE 0 END) as ltv_7days,
        SUM(CASE WHEN hours_after_first <= 720 THEN amount ELSE 0 END) as ltv_30days
    FROM customer_payments_with_hours
    GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT 
    AVG(cwp.ltv_7days / cl.total_ltv * 100.0) as avg_pct_7days,
    AVG(cwp.ltv_30days / cl.total_ltv * 100.0) as avg_pct_30days,
    AVG(cl.total_ltv) as avg_ltv
FROM customer_ltv cl
JOIN customer_window_payments cwp ON cl.customer_id = cwp.customer_id
